mainTopic: Saving life on שבת: medicine, a later שבת, acting quickly, and not following the רוב in פיקוח נפש
overview: First, the גמרא proves from a ברייתא of רבה בר שמואל, and from the wording of the משנה (רב אשי), that the חכמים agree with רבי מתיא בן חרש: medicine may be put in a sick mouth on שבת. Next, רב teaches that the משנה's line 'וכל ספק נפשות דוחה את השבת' covers danger on a later שבת too. So an eight-day treatment that starts on שבת begins right away, even though a second שבת will be broken. A ברייתא about heating water for the sick supports this. It also teaches that leading Jews should do the work, and explains whose opinion counts in deciding it is needed. Another ברייתא teaches that the one who is quick to save a life on שבת is praised and needs no permission from בית דין. It gives four examples: a child in the sea, a child in a pit, a child behind a locked door, and a fire. The גמרא explains why each case is needed. Then שמואל rules that in פיקוח נפש we do not follow the רוב. The גמרא works out his case, a person who left the group for another courtyard, and squares it with רבי יוחנן. Finally, it challenges שמואל from the משנה about an abandoned baby, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא with three cases and a short reply from the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא taught by רבה בר שמואל. It lists three rulings of רבי מתיא בן חרש, and the חכמים answer, 'In this one and not in the others.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what רבה בר שמואל taught. A pregnant woman who smells food and craves it: we feed her until she feels settled. Someone bitten by a mad dog: we feed him the lobe of the dog's liver. Someone with pain in his mouth: we put medicine in his mouth on שבת. These are the words of רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, who said them in the name of רבי מתיא בן חרש. The חכמים say: in this one, and not in the others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer its open question: do the חכמים disagree about medicine on שבת? The proof is not clear yet, because we still need to work out which case 'בזו' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives three cases from one source. The חכמים agree to exactly one of them and reject the rest. If we can work out which case 'this one' is, we will know whether they agree about the medicine.

keyTerms.meaning: A pregnant woman who smelled food and craves it
One who has pain in his mouth

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabba bar Shmuel taught:
A pregnant woman who smelled food —
we feed her until her spirit is restored,
and one whom a mad dog bit —
we feed him from the lobe of its liver,
and one who has pain in his mouth —
we put medicine in for him on Shabbat,
these are the words of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מַתְיָא בֶּן חָרָשׁ.
phrases.english: who said it in the name of Rabbi Matya ben Charash.
And the Sages say: in this one and not in another.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised on the previous amud: do the חכמים argue with רבי מתיא בן חרש about medicine?
steps.raayaObject: Whether the חכמים agree that medicine may be put in a sick mouth on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבה בר שמואל

steps.title: Which case does 'this one' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the three cases the חכמים meant when they said 'בזו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In this one': which case does it refer to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'this one' points to. It is setting up the next move, where it rules out one possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on this single word. Until we know which case the חכמים agreed to, the ברייתא proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: On which one? Which case does it refer to?

phrases.english: 'In this one': to which does it refer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the wording of the ברייתא's last line means
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three cases 'בזו' refers to

steps.title: It cannot mean the pregnant woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that 'בזו' means the pregnant woman, because no one argues about her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the pregnant woman, that is obvious! Is there anyone who says we do not feed a pregnant woman?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out the pregnant woman as the meaning of 'this one'. Everyone already agrees she is fed, so the חכמים would not need to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים' words must be telling us something new. Feeding a pregnant woman who craves food is agreed by everyone, so it makes no sense to single it out. That leaves the medicine as the likely case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say it refers to the pregnant woman, it is obvious!

phrases.aramaic: עוּבָּרָה מִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּלָא?
phrases.english: A pregnant woman: is there anyone who says no?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one possible answer to the question and rejects it
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חכמים would be saying something obvious, since everyone agrees she is fed

steps.title: So it means the medicine, and the חכמים agree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'בזו' refers to the medicine. So the חכמים agree with רבי מתיא בן חרש on this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, does it not refer to the medicine? Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the חכמים agree about the medicine. This answers the open question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pregnant woman is ruled out, and the liver of a mad dog is the case the חכמים reject. So 'this one' must be the medicine. The חכמים allow putting medicine in a sick mouth on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that...? (leads to a conclusion)
Learn from it: the proof stands

phrases.english: Rather, is it not referring to the medicine?
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion now that the other reading has been rejected
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חכמים agree with רבי מתיא בן חרש that medicine may be put in a sick mouth on שבת

steps.title: רב אשי: the משנה's wording points the same way
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה's own wording supports this answer. It brings the medicine ruling separately with 'ועוד', and no argument from the חכמים follows it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: the משנה is also precise this way. It says, 'And furthermore, רבי מתיא בן חרש said: one who has pain in his mouth, we put medicine in for him on שבת.' And the חכמים do not argue with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a second proof, this time from how the משנה is worded. He notes that the חכמים do not argue on the medicine ruling, and he explains why in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the חכמים' argument comes right after the mad-dog ruling. The medicine ruling comes afterward, introduced by 'ועוד', and no argument follows it. רב אשי reads this order as a sign that the חכמים agree about the medicine.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה's wording also shows this

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Our mishna is also precise this way —

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי מַתְיָא בֶּן חָרָשׁ:
phrases.english: 'And furthermore, Rabbi Matya ben Charash said:

phrases.aramaic: הַחוֹשֵׁשׁ בְּפִיו מְטִילִין לוֹ סַם בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: one who has pain in his mouth, we put medicine in for him on Shabbat,'
and the Rabbis do not argue with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof, from the משנה, for the same conclusion
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים agree about medicine on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order and wording of the משנה

steps.title: If they argued, the משנה would have grouped the rulings together
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains his proof. If the חכמים disagreed about the medicine too, the משנה would have listed both rulings together and put one argument at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were true that the חכמים argue with him, the משנה should have combined both rulings and taught them together. Then the חכמים would argue in the last part. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his proof. The way the משנה is arranged shows that the חכמים only argued about the mad dog.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה naturally groups rulings that share the same argument. Here the חכמים' argument is placed only after the mad-dog ruling, and the medicine comes separately with no argument. So they must agree about the medicine.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it combine them and teach them together
The last part (of a משנה or ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: Two proofs, the ברייתא of רבה בר שמואל and the wording of the משנה, both show the same thing. The חכמים agree that medicine may be put in a sick mouth on שבת. They only reject the mad-dog liver cure.

phrases.english: And if it were so that the Rabbis argue with him,
let it combine them and teach them together,
and let the Rabbis argue in the last clause.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רב אשי's observation proves the point, and closes the topic
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's structure confirms that the חכמים agree about medicine on שבת

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the extra line about ספק נפשות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's reason, 'because it is ספק נפשות'. It asks why the משנה also adds 'וכל ספק נפשות דוחה את השבת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says, 'Because it is ספק נפשות, etc.' Why do I need it to say further: 'And any ספק נפשות overrides שבת'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic in the משנה. It asks why the general rule is added when the reason was already given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said medicine is allowed because there may be danger to life. Repeating 'any ספק נפשות overrides שבת' seems to add nothing. The גמרא assumes every phrase must teach something new.

phrases.english: 'Because it is a case of possible danger to life,' etc.
Why do I need it to say further:
'And any case of possible danger to life overrides Shabbat'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next words of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra general rule adds to the reason the משנה already gave

steps.title: רב: the rule also covers danger on a later שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב explains the extra line. We break שבת not only for danger on this שבת, but even for possible danger on a later שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: they did not say this only about a doubt on this שבת. They said it even about a doubt on another שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains what the extra line adds. It stretches the rule to cover danger on a future שבת as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first phrase, 'it is ספק נפשות', covers danger right now. The general rule teaches more: we break this שבת even when the worry involves a later שבת. The next steps show what kind of case this means.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not say this only...

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא סָפֵק שַׁבָּת זוֹ בִּלְבַד אָמְרוּ,
phrases.english: They did not say it only about a doubt on this Shabbat,
but even about a doubt on another Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the extra line is needed
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra line teaches that ספק נפשות overrides שבת even when the doubt involves a future שבת
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that פיקוח נפש is not limited to the danger in front of us. We act right away even when the danger connects to a later שבת.

steps.title: What would such a case look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a real example of a doubt about another שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a practical example of רב's rule. It is setting up the case that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Doubt about another שבת' is hard to picture. A concrete case will make the rule clear.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an example of רב's rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real case of a doubt about another שבת

steps.title: An eight-day treatment that starts on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The case: doctors judge that a sick person needs eight days of treatment, and the first day is שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, they judged that he needs treatment for eight days, and the first day is שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the case. An eight-day treatment that starts on שבת will run into a second שבת at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If treatment starts on שבת, day eight lands on the next שבת, so two שבתות are broken. If it started right after שבת, the eight days would run from Sunday to the next Sunday, so only the one שבת in the middle would be broken. This is where the doubt about 'another שבת' comes in.

phrases.english: For example, where they judged that he needs eight days,
and the first day is Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a case
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An eight-day treatment whose first day is שבת

steps.title: Do not wait until after שבת to save a second שבת
steps.stepSummary: One might think we should wait until שבת is over so that only one שבת is broken. רב's rule teaches that we start treatment right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let him wait until evening, so that we do not break two שבתות for him. So it teaches us that we do not wait.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the mistaken idea that the rule comes to reject. We might think we should wait so that fewer שבתות are broken. The rule teaches that we treat him immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Waiting looks like it protects שבת, because it saves a second שבת from being broken. But any delay puts the sick person at risk. Saving a life comes first, even if this means breaking more שבתות overall.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea)

steps.whatToRemember: The line 'וכל ספק נפשות דוחה את השבת' teaches that we treat a person in danger right away on שבת. This holds even if starting now means a second שבת will also be broken.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the point is to keep the number of broken שבתות as low as possible. The rule is the opposite: we start treatment at once and do not delay to protect a later שבת.

phrases.english: You might have said:
let him wait until evening,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא נֵיחוּל עֲלֵיהּ תְּרֵי שַׁבָּתָא,
phrases.english: so that we not desecrate two Shabbatot for him;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what mistake the rule prevents in the case just described
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We break שבת right away for a sick person in danger, even if this causes a second שבת to be broken. We do not wait until after שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic halachic rule for treating the sick on שבת: we do not delay treatment to reduce how much שבת is broken.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב: heat water right away, even for a future שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same thing as רב. We heat water for a sick person on שבת right away and do not wait, because even possible danger on a later שבת pushes aside שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: We heat water for a sick person on שבת, either for him to drink or to wash him. They did not say this only about this שבת, but also about another שבת. We do not say, 'Let us wait, maybe he will get better.' Instead, we heat it for him right away, because ספק נפשות pushes aside שבת. And this is not only a doubt about this שבת, but even a doubt about another שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב said in Step 8, as support for his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב taught that even possible danger on a future שבת allows breaking this שבת. The ברייתא says the same thing in almost the same words, so רב's rule now has an older source behind it. It also adds a practical warning: do not delay treatment hoping the sick person will recover by himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא brought as support)
To wash him or make him healthy
A doubt about danger to life

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical rule that we start life-saving treatment on שבת right away. We do not push it off to reduce the number of שבתות that are broken.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
We heat hot water for a sick person on Shabbat,
whether to give him to drink or to wash him.
And they did not say this only about this Shabbat,
but even about another Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אוֹמְרִים: נַמְתִּין לוֹ שֶׁמָּא יַבְרִיא,
phrases.english: And we do not say: Let us wait for him, maybe he will get well,
rather, we heat it for him right away,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁסְּפֵק נְפָשׁוֹת דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: because a doubt about life pushes aside Shabbat.
And not only a doubt about this Shabbat,
but even a doubt about another Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an older source that matches רב's rule about a future שבת
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that even possible danger on a later שבת pushes aside this שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about heating water for a sick person, which uses nearly the same wording

steps.title: Who should do the life-saving work
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: these acts should not be given to non-Jews or כותים. The leading Jews should do them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not do these things through non-Jews or through כותים. Instead, they are done by the great ones of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a new point: who should actually do the work of breaking שבת to save a life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think it is better to hand the work to someone who does not keep שבת. The ברייתא says no. Respected Jews should do it themselves, so that everyone learns that saving a life on שבת is fully permitted and is not something to avoid.

keyTerms.meaning: The great or leading people of ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean breaking שבת here is a lesser kind of sin that we try to avoid. The point is the opposite: the most respected people do it, to show it is fully permitted.

phrases.english: And we do not do these things
not through gentiles,
and not through Samaritans,
but through the great ones of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a rule about who does the work
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Life-saving work on שבת should be done by leading Jews, not handed off to non-Jews or כותים

steps.title: Whose opinion can decide that the work is needed
steps.stepSummary: Women or כותים alone cannot decide that these acts must be done. Their opinion can still join together with another opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not say 'these things should be done' based on the word of women or כותים. But their opinion does join together with another opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now discusses whose judgment can start the process of breaking שבת for a sick person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At that time, these people were not treated as recognized medical experts. So their opinion alone cannot decide that the sick person needs שבת to be broken. But if experts are unsure or disagree, their view counts and can help tip the decision.

keyTerms.meaning: They join together (their opinion is counted)

phrases.english: And we do not say these things should be done
not based on women,
and not based on Samaritans,
but they join together with another opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who does the work to whose opinion can start it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women or כותים alone cannot decide that שבת should be broken, but their view joins another opinion
steps.whatToRemember: The first ברייתא teaches three things. We treat right away, even for a future שבת. Leading Jews do the work. And the decision rests on recognized opinions, though other voices can join in.

steps.title: General rule: save lives on שבת quickly, without asking בית דין
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that we save lives on שבת, the one who is quick is praised, and no permission from בית דין is needed. It then asks 'how so?' to set up examples.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: We save a life on שבת. Whoever is quick about it is praiseworthy, and he does not need to get permission from בית דין. How so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a general rule about פיקוח נפש on שבת. It ends with 'how so?', which sets up the examples that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא adds two new points. Speed is praised, not just allowed. And a person should act on his own, because waiting to ask בית דין could cost a life.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
We engage in saving a life on Shabbat,
and the one who is quick is praiseworthy,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לִיטּוֹל רְשׁוּת מִבֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: and he does not need to take permission from the court.
How so?
phrases.notes: Setup question that opens the list of examples

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְפַקְּחִין פִּקּוּחַ נֶפֶשׁ בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא on the same theme of saving life on שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saving a life on שבת should be done quickly, and the one who is quick is praised without needing permission from בית דין

steps.title: Example one: a child in the sea, even though fish are caught too
steps.stepSummary: If a child falls into the sea, we spread a net and pull him up without asking permission. The גמרא adds: this is true even though fish are caught in the net at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sees a child who fell into the sea, he spreads a net and pulls him up. Whoever is quick is praiseworthy, and he does not need permission from בית דין. And this is so even though he is also catching fish.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first example answering 'how so?'. Then the גמרא adds its own short Aramaic note about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spreading a net is normally the forbidden work of trapping (צידה). The added note teaches something new. Even though fish get caught along with the child, which brings an extra forbidden act and even a side benefit, he should still rescue right away.
steps.confusionAlert: The lines starting with וְאַף עַל גַּב are the גמרא's Aramaic additions, not part of the Hebrew ברייתא.

phrases.english: If he saw a child who fell into the sea,
he spreads a net and brings him up,
and the one who is quick is praiseworthy,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לִיטּוֹל רְשׁוּת מִבֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: and he does not need to take permission from the court.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקָא צָיֵיד כְּווֹרֵי.
phrases.english: And even though he is catching fish.
phrases.notes: This line is the גמרא adding its own words, in Aramaic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers 'how so?' with the first example
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the general rule of quick rescue looks in real cases
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Spread a net to save a drowning child, even though fish are caught along with him

steps.title: Example two: a child in a pit, even though a step is made
steps.stepSummary: If a child falls into a pit, we dig out a piece of the edge and pull him up. The גמרא adds: this is true even though doing so makes a usable step.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sees a child who fell into a pit, he pulls out a section of the ground and brings him up. Whoever is quick is praiseworthy, and he does not need permission from בית דין. This is so even though he is making a step.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second example of the rule, again followed by the גמרא's short Aramaic note.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Digging out part of the ground is normally forbidden work. The note adds that even though he ends up making a lasting step, which is like building something useful, he should still rescue right away.

keyTerms.meaning: He uproots a section (of earth at the pit's edge)

phrases.english: If he saw a child who fell into a pit,
he uproots a section of earth and brings him up,
and the one who is quick is praiseworthy,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לִיטּוֹל רְשׁוּת מִבֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: and he does not need to take permission from the court.
Even though he fashions a step.
phrases.notes: This line is the גמרא adding its own words, in Aramaic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second example in the same list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dig out earth to save a child from a pit, even though a usable step is made

steps.title: Example three: a child behind a locked door, even if he wants the boards
steps.stepSummary: If a door is locked in front of a child, we break it and take him out. The גמרא adds: this is true even if he means to break it into boards he can use.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sees that a door was locked in front of a child, he breaks it and takes him out. Whoever is quick is praiseworthy, and he does not need permission from בית דין. This is so even though he intends to break it into useful boards.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third example, with the גמרא's note added at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the note goes a step further. It is not just that a side benefit happens by accident. Even if the rescuer actually wants the boards, the rescue is still permitted and praised.

phrases.english: If he saw that a door was locked before a child,
he breaks it and takes him out,
and the one who is quick is praiseworthy,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לִיטּוֹל רְשׁוּת מִבֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: and he does not need to take permission from the court.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקָא מִיכַּוֵּין לְמִיתְבַּר בְּשִׁיפֵי.
phrases.english: And even though he intends to break it into boards.
phrases.notes: This line is the גמרא adding its own words, in Aramaic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third example in the same list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Break a door to free a trapped child, even if he also wants the boards

steps.title: Example four: putting out a fire, even though coals are produced
steps.stepSummary: We put out and block a fire on שבת when life is in danger, without asking permission. The גמרא adds: this is true even though usable coals are left over.
steps.simpleTranslation: We put out a fire and block it on שבת. Whoever is quick is praiseworthy, and he does not need permission from בית דין. This is so even though he is producing coals.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the fourth and last example in the list, again with the גמרא's short note.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting out a fire is normally the forbidden work of extinguishing (מכבה). The note teaches that even though the half-burned wood becomes coals he can use after שבת, he should still act right away to protect lives.

keyTerms.meaning: We block it off with a barrier

steps.whatToRemember: In all four cases, saving a life comes first and should be done quickly, with no permission needed. This is true even when the rescue also involves more forbidden work or brings the rescuer some side benefit.

phrases.english: We extinguish and block off because of a fire on Shabbat,
and the one who is quick is praiseworthy,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לִיטּוֹל רְשׁוּת מִבֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: and he does not need to take permission from the court.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקָא מְמַכֵּיךְ מַכּוֹכֵי.
phrases.english: And even though he produces coals.
phrases.notes: This line is the גמרא adding its own words, in Aramaic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth example in the same list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Put out a dangerous fire on שבת right away, even though usable coals are produced

steps.title: Why both the sea case and the pit case are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the pit case adds something the sea case does not. With the sea, you must rush because the child gets swept away. With a pit, the child just sits there, so we might think you should wait for permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If it had only taught us the sea, we would say that is because in the meantime the child gets swept away. But a pit, where the child just sits there, I would say no. So it is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a צריכותא, explaining why the ברייתא needed to list more than one rescue case. Here it shows why the pit case had to be added to the sea case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the sea, every second counts because the child can drift away. So acting without asking בית דין seems obvious there. In a pit, the child is not going anywhere, so we might think there is time to ask permission. The ברייתא teaches the pit case to tell us: no, do not wait there either.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (each case teaches something new)

steps.confusionAlert: The צריכותא is not saying the pit case is less serious. It is ruling out a mistaken reason to delay, namely that there is time to ask permission.

phrases.english: And it is necessary (to list each case):
for if it had taught us only the sea —
that is because in the meantime he is swept away,
but a pit, where he stays sitting —
I would say no (wait for permission); so it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at the ברייתא's list of cases (steps 16–19) and explains why the pit case is not redundant after the sea case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when the danger is not getting worse every second (a pit), you still rescue right away without asking permission.

steps.title: Why both the pit case and the locked door case are needed
steps.stepSummary: The pit case alone might be explained by the child being scared. Behind a locked door, someone could calm the child with nuts until שבת ends. So the door case is needed to teach that you still break in right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had only taught us the pit, that is because the child is frightened. But a locked door, where one could sit on this side and amuse him with nuts, I would say no. So it is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The צריכותא continues, showing why the locked door case had to be added after the pit case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child in a pit is terrified, and fear itself can be dangerous. That might be why we rush there. Behind a locked door, someone could stay on the other side and keep the child calm by rattling nuts until שבת is over. The ברייתא still says to break the door right away, so we do not rely on calming the child.
steps.whatToRemember: Each rescue case removes another excuse to delay: the danger is not growing, or the child can be calmed. In every case we act at once.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only the pit —
that is because he is frightened,
but when a door is locked (in front of him),
it is possible to sit on this side (of the door)
and amuse him with nuts.
So it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second link of the same צריכותא: pit compared with locked door.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even if the child could be kept calm until after שבת, we break the door immediately.

steps.title: Why is the fire case listed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's fire case and asks what new point it adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'We extinguish and cut off a fire.' Why do I need this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the fire line from the ברייתא and asks why it is needed. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already taught that we break שבת to save a life. The fire case was not explained in the צריכותא, so it seems to add nothing new. The גמרא asks what it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: We cut off or block (the fire's spread)
Why do I need it? (asking what a line adds)

phrases.english: 'We extinguish and block (a fire).'
Why do I need this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the first three cases, the גמרא turns to the fourth case, the fire, which was not covered.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point does the fire case add beyond the earlier rescue cases?

steps.title: Even to protect another courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The fire case teaches that we may put out or block the fire even to stop it from reaching people in a different courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: To teach that this applies even to (stop it from spreading to) another courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the fire case adds that we may fight the fire even when it threatens people in another courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought we only break שבת for people right in front of the danger. The fire case widens the rule: even if the people in danger are in the next courtyard, we put out or block the fire. The danger does not have to be right here and now.
steps.whatToRemember: פיקוח נפש covers a danger that is spreading toward others, not only a person who is already in danger.

phrases.english: That (we may do so) even for another courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the 'why do I need it' question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fire case teaches that we may fight the fire even to protect people in another courtyard.

steps.title: שמואל: in saving a life we do not follow the majority
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, quoting רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, teaches that in פיקוח נפש we do not follow the רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said that רב יהודה said that שמואל said: In saving a life, they did not follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens a new topic: what to do in a doubtful case where the majority would point away from saving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when something is unclear, הלכה goes by the רוב. שמואל says that when a life might be at stake, we do not use the רוב to decide not to save. Even a small chance of a life at risk is enough to break שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not follow the majority

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shows how seriously הלכה takes even a small chance of saving a life.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They did not go, in saving a life,
after the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא's rescue cases to a new rule about doubtful cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In פיקוח נפש, we do not use the majority to decide against saving.

steps.title: What case does שמואל mean? Not nine Jews and one גוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case שמואל is talking about. It rules out a group of nine Jews and one גוי, since there the majority is Jewish and saving follows the רוב anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say there are nine Jews and one גוי among them, the majority are Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact case of שמואל's rule. It tests a first possibility and rules it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case discussed, a building collapses on one person from a group. If nine of ten are Jews, the person is most likely Jewish, so going by the רוב already tells us to save. That cannot be what שמואל meant by 'not following the majority.'

phrases.english: What is the case?
If we say there are nine Jews
and one gentile among them —
the majority are Jews (so we are following the majority),

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִי נֵימָא דְּאִיכָּא תִּשְׁעָה יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case שמואל's rule refers to and rejects the first suggestion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case does 'not following the majority' really apply?

steps.title: Not half and half either: that is a plain doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules out a half-Jewish, half-gentile group too. That is an even doubt, and we are already lenient in ספק נפשות, so there is no majority being ignored.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, half and half? A doubt about a life is treated leniently (and that is not ignoring a majority either).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests a second possibility, a half-and-half group, and rules it out as well. The next step offers a new suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an even split, there is no majority at all. It is simply a ספק נפשות, which we already know is treated leniently, so we save. Since no majority is being ignored, this cannot be שמואל's case either.

keyTerms.meaning: To be lenient (here: break שבת to save)

steps.confusionAlert: 'לְהָקֵל' here means being lenient about breaking שבת, so we do save. It does not mean being lenient by not saving.

phrases.english: (Rather,) half and half?
A doubt regarding life is ruled leniently (and that is not ignoring a majority).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second suggested case, also rejected. The search for שמואל's case continues.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out the half-and-half case as the meaning of שמואל's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no majority in an even split, and ספק נפשות already leads to saving, so the case is not an example of ignoring the רוב.

steps.title: Suggesting a case of nine gentiles and one Jew
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting the first two cases, the גמרא suggests that שמואל means a group of nine gentiles and one Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be where there are nine gentiles and one Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third possible case for שמואל's rule: mostly gentiles with only one Jew. This sets up the next step, where the suggestion will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the majority is gentile, so here 'not following the רוב' would actually change the outcome. That makes this case look like a good fit for שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new suggestion after rejecting earlier ones)

phrases.english: Rather, where there are
nine gentiles and one Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאִיכָּא תִּשְׁעָה גּוֹיִם וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new case after steps 25-26 rejected nine-Jews-one-gentile and half-and-half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case does שמואל's rule address?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Suggestion: a group of nine gentiles and one Jew.

steps.title: That case is also obvious, because a fixed group counts as half and half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. A group in a fixed place is treated like an even 50/50 doubt, so of course we save.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also obvious! The group is in a fixed place (קבוע), and anything in a fixed place is treated like half and half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: we do not need שמואל to teach this case. There is already a known rule that settles it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of קבוע, when the doubt comes up while everyone is still in their fixed spot, we do not count the majority. We treat it as a 50/50 doubt. A 50/50 doubt about a life already means we save (step 26), so שמואל's rule would add nothing new here.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (why would we need this taught?)
Fixed in place; a group whose items are still in their set location
It is treated like half and half (an even doubt)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'nine gentiles' means the majority decides. Because the group is קבוע, the numbers are ignored, and it is treated as an even 50/50 doubt.

phrases.english: This too is obvious,
because it is a fixed group,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל קָבוּעַ כְּמֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה דָּמֵי!
phrases.english: and anything fixed is treated as half and half!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion of step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The case of nine gentiles and one Jew all in one courtyard.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule of קבוע already makes it a 50/50 doubt, so שמואל's rule teaches nothing new there.

steps.title: The case is one person who left for another courtyard
steps.stepSummary: שמואל is needed where someone separated from the group and went to another courtyard. We might have said he came from the gentile majority, so שמואל teaches that we still save him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed where one person separated and went to another courtyard. You might have thought: whoever separates came from the majority (so he is probably a gentile). So שמואל teaches us that in פיקוח נפש we do not follow the רוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally finds a case where שמואל's rule adds something: a person who left the group and was trapped somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once someone leaves the fixed group, the rule of קבוע no longer covers him. A different rule would normally apply: כל דפריש מרובא פריש, meaning what leaves comes from the majority. That rule would make him 'probably a gentile.' שמואל teaches that for saving a life we ignore that majority and still dig him out on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (this case)
Where he separated / left the group
Whatever separates is assumed to come from the majority

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the basic difference between קבוע (still in place, so it is 50/50) and פריש (separated, so we normally follow the majority). It also shows that פיקוח נפש overrides even the פריש majority.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where he separated to another courtyard.
You might have said:
whatever separates, separates from the majority.
So it teaches us

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא הָלְכוּ בְּפִקּוּחַ נֶפֶשׁ אַחַר הָרוֹב.
phrases.english: that in saving a life we do not follow the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' objection of step 28 by moving the case out of the fixed courtyard.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A person who separated is assumed to come from the gentile majority, so we would not dig him out on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: In פיקוח נפש we ignore even the majority of פריש and save him.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says we do not dig in another courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this using רבי יוחנן: with nine gentiles and one Jew, we dig in the same courtyard, but not in another courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: nine gentiles and one Jew in that same courtyard, we dig him out. In another courtyard, we do not dig him out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 29 with a statement of רבי יוחנן that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says that in another courtyard we do not dig. That seems to mean we do follow the 'separated from the majority' rule there. This clashes with the claim that שמואל saves even in another courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: We clear away the rubble (to save him)

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Asi say in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
nine gentiles and one Jew,
in that same courtyard, we clear the rubble;
in another courtyard, we do not clear the rubble!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case set up in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that in another courtyard we save, ignoring the majority.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן explicitly says that in another courtyard we do not dig.

steps.title: It depends on whether all of them left or only some
steps.stepSummary: No contradiction: if the whole group moved to the other courtyard, we save. If only some of them moved, we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. This case (we save) is where they all moved. That case (we do not save) is where only some of them moved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the clash by splitting the 'other courtyard' situation into two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole group moved, the Jew was surely among those who left. So the person trapped in the other courtyard may well be the Jew. Even though the majority are gentiles, שמואל's rule says we ignore that majority and save him. If only some of them left, the Jew may never have left the first courtyard at all, so רבי יוחנן says we do not dig. שמואל and רבי יוחנן are talking about different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (there is no contradiction)

steps.whatToRemember: Fixed group (קבוע): treat it as 50/50, so we save. One who separated: normally he follows the majority, but שמואל says in פיקוח נפש we still save. If the whole group moved, we save. If only part of the group moved, we do not dig (רבי יוחנן).

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where all of them moved,
that is where only some of them moved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל and רבי יוחנן contradict each other about the other courtyard.
steps.terutzMaskana: Whole group moved: we save. Only some moved: we do not dig.

steps.title: Challenge from the abandoned baby משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל really said this. It quotes the משנה that an abandoned baby follows the city's majority, along with רב's statement that this ruling is about keeping the child alive. The challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did שמואל really say this? But we learned in a משנה: if one found an abandoned baby there, if most of the city are gentiles, he is a gentile. If most are Jews, he is a Jew. If it is half and half, he is a Jew. And רב said: they taught this only for keeping him alive, but not for his family status (יחוס).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to שמואל's rule. It brings a משנה that seems to follow the majority, plus רב's comment on it. The full force of the attack is spelled out on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that in a mostly-gentile city the baby is treated as a gentile, which sounds like following the רוב. רב's comment connects that ruling to keeping the child alive. Together, this suggests that the majority does decide matters of life, which seems to conflict with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: To keep him alive / provide for his survival
To establish his lineage (for marriage status)

steps.confusionAlert: רב's line is not the answer to the challenge. It is part of the quoted material that the גמרא is using to build the challenge against שמואל.

phrases.english: Did Shmuel really say this?
But we learned: if one found an abandoned baby in it (the city),
if the majority are gentiles, he is a gentile;
and if the majority are Jews, he is a Jew;
if half and half, he is a Jew.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְהַחְיוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: And Rav said: they taught this only regarding keeping him alive,
but not regarding his lineage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining שמואל's case to challenging his rule from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that in פיקוח נפש we do not follow the רוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules by the majority in a mostly-gentile city, and רב ties that ruling to keeping the child alive. This seems to show the majority decides matters of life. The challenge continues on the next amud.
